done_when: A Claude worker's fix round continues the session its first round started and gets only the short fix prompt; when that session can't be continued it starts fresh with the full brief and says so; tests run forge work twice on a Claude worker and check both paths

findings.body: Every nonzero exit from `--resume` increments `failed_resumes`, whether Claude rejected the session or accepted it and failed during the turn. An explicit “No conversation found” rejection leaves that fix round failed; Forge tries the same unusable session in the next round and starts fresh only in the third. Conversely, two failed turns in a valid session cause Forge to discard its context and send the full brief. Claude documents a missing session as a distinct resume error, so exit status alone cannot justify either decision. Handle a confirmed resume rejection in that fix round and retain the session after ordinary turn failures. See the [Claude Code error reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors).

findings.body: This test expects two failed `forge work` calls after the stub rejects `--resume`, then checks a fresh session on a third call. It therefore passes while the required fix round fails instead of restarting with the full brief and an explanation. Test the rejection on the second `forge work` call and assert its fresh session, full brief, and reason.

findings.body: The test makes one accepted resume fail and then succeed; its two-consecutive-failure case deletes the stub’s session first. It never exercises two failed turns while the session remains resumable. In that case, the next `forge work` starts a new session because of the counter at `worker.py:96`. Keep the stub session registered through two failing resumed turns and assert that the following round still sends the short prompt with `--resume`.

why: Claude workers start a fresh session every round and get the whole brief again, so fix rounds lose the worker's context, unlike Codex workers
